scope: One year; distributed responsibility for instrumentation versus centralized injector/operator. Fourteen of eighteen demo services support the payload; exclude one common direct pilot. Initial centralized enrollment is one policy operation per independent rollout domain, with no per-service setup allowance. OBI deployment is a one-time 30-minute planning assumption supplied by the presenter, not a measured result. Agent releases occur monthly (12/year); each distributed service owner performs one update, while the centralized platform performs one shared update per domain. Shared release qualification common to both approaches cancels; any different compatibility or exception effort must be entered separately. All labor durations and domain counts are hypothetical planning inputs. No per-investigation saving is credited once equivalent instrumentation exists. No telemetry-volume, dynamic enable/disable, waiting-time, outage-revenue or cash-saving credit is assumed. RIO is a talk-specific demo; prototype development/hardening and extra support/telemetry costs need explicit estimates.
